decisions.question: USO-Q1 mechanism: how a base PERMIT drops out when an exception closes the type list
decisions.recommendation: (A) R-BZ data plus one evaluator read: a vocab block exception_type_list_closure declares all 19 "only"-list closures, and permitted() reads it in one place; on a lot whose exception is in the block, a base-layer permission that is not a listed type is not a use subject on this lot, and the other classes read not_evaluated:no_candidate with the closed disclosure "Exception <n> permits only <types>". A checkVocab arm validates each key (a 900.x exception) and each type (a building_type). Cost: one evaluator rule (moves evaluator_version), a vocab block and the checkVocab arm. Rule text changed (disclosed): the mechanism wording of CHAT-194.USO-Q1 becomes "applied as declared data read by permitted()"; keying cannot drop a base PERMIT because displaces[] is generated, never keyed (xref.mjs:9).

decisions.question: USO-Q1: which base type list the closure reaches
decisions.recommendation: The closure reaches 10.x.20.40(1) only. 10.x.20.40(2) permits the houseplex "despite 900.1.10(3)/(4)(A)", i.e. despite exceptions, and stays as the by-law text says. Cost: none beyond USO-Q1e. The alternative, closing (2) too, contradicts the clause's own "Despite" wording and changes 12 sample lot-classes.
